speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a serious finding that requires immediate attention. To start our evaluation, how many days old are you, and have you passed meconium stool yet?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus.

The history of bilious vomiting in a newborn born six hours after delivery is a surgical emergency. The lack of meconium passage and the family history of pyloric stenosis raise concern for anatomical anomalies. I am requesting an emergent upper gastrointestinal (UGI) series to confirm the diagnosis.
